rule: Do not re-query DatasetDagRunQueue (or any table already loaded into memory) inside the per-DAG scheduler loop; pass already-fetched data through instead to avoid N+1 queries.
trigger: A new session.scalars() or session.execute() call targeting DatasetDagRunQueue appears inside a for-loop that iterates over dags_needing_dagruns or dataset_triggered_dag_info.
rationale: dags_needing_dagruns already loads all DDRQ records; re-fetching per DAG adds one query per dataset-triggered DAG per scheduler loop tick, and accessing .dataset.uri without eager loading compounds this into an N+1 pattern.

evidence.excerpt: Re-fetching adds one query per dataset-triggered DAG per scheduler loop

rule: When eager-loading is absent on a SQLAlchemy relationship used inside the scheduler loop, do not access that relationship attribute lazily; either add eager loading or pass the data from the outer query.
trigger: A scheduler-loop function accesses a dotted relationship attribute (e.g. record.dataset.uri) on a model where the relationship is not declared with lazy='joined' or joinedload().
rationale: Lazy loads inside the scheduler loop produce an N+1 query pattern that degrades scheduler throughput under load.

evidence.excerpt: r.dataset.uri triggers a lazy load per record — N+1 query pattern

rule: Each upload-artifact step in a GitHub Actions workflow must use a unique artifact name; never reuse the same name (including names that share a dynamic suffix) across multiple upload steps in the same job.
trigger: Two or more actions/upload-artifact steps within the same job share the same `name:` value or the same name template (e.g. both use container-logs-${{env.JOB_ID}}).
rationale: Duplicate artifact names cause silent overwrites or upload collisions depending on runner artifact settings.

evidence.excerpt: Duplicate name can overwrite or collide depending on artifact settings

rule: Do not include unrelated uv.lock churn in a feature or fix PR; either revert lock-file changes or split them into a separate commit with a stated reason tied to the PR.
trigger: uv.lock appears in the diff of a PR whose description does not mention a dependency bump, and the lock diff is larger than a few lines.
rationale: Unexplained lock-file churn obscures the actual change, inflates review noise, and may introduce unintended dependency upgrades.

evidence.excerpt: 362 lines of churn looks unrelated; revert or split with clear reason

rule: Task-SDK client changelog entries must appear in the Task-SDK changelog, not in the core airflow-core RELEASE_NOTES.rst.
trigger: RELEASE_NOTES.rst receives a line mentioning 'task-sdk', 'task SDK', or 'Task SDK client' in a section that belongs to airflow-core.
rationale: The server/client separation means task-sdk has its own release cadence; mixing entries blurs the boundary and confuses downstream consumers of each package.

evidence.excerpt: task-sdk client entry expected in task sdk changelog, not core

rule: A database migration included in a patch release must only repair a bug in an existing migration; it must not change payload semantics so that users who already ran the original upgrade end up in a different state from a fresh installer.
trigger: A patch-release PR modifies a file under migrations/ (or alembic/versions/) and the diff touches both upgrade() and downgrade() logic beyond simple no-op corrections.
rationale: Divergent DB state between upgraders and fresh installers is a data-integrity hazard that is very hard to recover from in production deployments.

evidence.excerpt: Confirm this only repairs a bug, not changing payload semantics

rule: Any new config option introduced in a patch release must be declared in config.yml and explicitly documented in the relevant upgrade notes for that minor version.
trigger: A patch PR adds a new key to config.yml or references a new [section] key_name in documentation without a corresponding entry in the upgrade notes.
rationale: Fresh config surface in a patch surprises operators who do not expect behavioural changes outside minor/major releases; the default value and its effect must be called out.

evidence.excerpt: Confirm config.yml schema is in sync; call out new default in upgrade docs

rule: A reusable workflow that has a committer allowlist on workflow_dispatch must apply the same allowlist check to its workflow_call trigger so that callers cannot bypass the gate.
trigger: A workflow file defines a committer-restricted workflow_dispatch block but also exposes a workflow_call trigger without an equivalent contains(fromJSON([...]), github.event.sender.login) guard.
rationale: Any workflow that calls the unguarded workflow_call path can bypass the explicit committer allowlist, defeating the access control.

evidence.excerpt: workflow_call input doesn't have the same committer restriction

rule: Provider policy documentation must not imply that a sponsoring committer is absolved of technical responsibility for PRs they merge; committers retain responsibility for CI health and security review regardless of steward approval.
trigger: PROVIDERS.rst (or equivalent governance doc) contains a sentence stating the sponsor is NOT responsible for the codebase or for merged PRs.
rationale: Committers have ASF-level obligations for every merge; a governance document that appears to waive that creates confusion about who is accountable for defects and security issues.

evidence.excerpt: Committer merging a PR should have responsibility to ensure it's technically ok

rule: Use vendor-neutral examples (e.g. the http provider) rather than named commercial vendors when illustrating provider policy concepts in governance documentation.
trigger: PROVIDERS.rst or a provider governance document uses a specific vendor name (e.g. Slack, AWS, GCP) as the sole illustrative example of a policy concept.
rationale: Vendor-named examples can appear to favour or implicitly endorse a particular commercial provider, which conflicts with the ASF vendor-neutrality principle.

evidence.excerpt: Maybe be a bit more vendor neutral and use http as example

rule: Every locale skill file under .github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/ must declare that it extends the global rules in ../SKILL.md, and must state that the locale file takes precedence over global rules on any conflict.
trigger: A new or modified locale skill file (.github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/<lang>.md) does not contain a reference to ../SKILL.md and a precedence statement.
rationale: Without an explicit inheritance declaration, AI translation agents may apply only the locale file and miss global guidance, leading to inconsistent translations across locales.

evidence.excerpt: Doesn't explicitly state it inherits global rules from ../SKILL.md

rule: In locale do-not-translate lists, mark only the bare Airflow noun (e.g. 'Asset') as untranslatable; do not block compound phrases (e.g. 'Asset Events') when existing translations already translate the surrounding words.
trigger: A locale skill file's do-not-translate list includes a multi-word phrase containing an Airflow term (e.g. 'Asset Events', 'Dag Run') when the existing locale JSON files translate the non-Airflow words in that phrase.
rationale: Blocking the full compound phrase contradicts established translations already in the codebase and produces inconsistency; only the proper noun component should be frozen.

evidence.excerpt: Existing pt locale strings translate concept as 'Evento(s) de Asset'

rule: Docs for extensible Airflow interfaces (state backends, secrets backends, etc.) must describe the contract and behaviour rather than listing concrete method signatures, which are subject to change.
trigger: A .rst documentation file adds a list-table or code-block containing full method signatures (async def ...) for a pluggable backend or extension point interface.
rationale: Concrete signatures in docs become stale when the interface evolves; the secrets-backend docs establish the precedent of describing what must be implemented without embedding signatures.

evidence.excerpt: Since these are signatures that can change, maybe do not mention at all

rule: CI shell scripts that start 'airflow standalone' in a polling loop must check process liveness with 'kill -0 $AIRFLOW_PID' to exit early when the process crashes instead of looping for the full timeout duration.
trigger: A CI shell script starts airflow standalone in the background, captures its PID, and then polls in a timed loop without a kill -0 $AIRFLOW_PID liveness check.
rationale: Without a liveness check the loop runs for the full timeout even if airflow standalone crashes immediately, wasting CI minutes and delaying failure feedback.

evidence.excerpt: Loop runs full 10 minutes even if process crashes after 1 second

rule: AIP skill SKILL.md files must anchor the AIP URL pattern to the Apache Confluence prefix (https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW) rather than a generic https:// host.
trigger: A SKILL.md under .github/skills/aip-* describes AIP URL detection as 'Other https:// arguments are the AIP URL' without anchoring to the cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW prefix.
rationale: Generic https:// matching cannot distinguish AIP URLs from arbitrary web links; the Confluence path prefix is the only reliable discriminator for valid AIP documents.

rule: Locale skill files must cross-reference the rationale documented in the corresponding airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/locales/<lang>/README.md when consolidating translation conventions.
trigger: A locale skill file under .github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/ is created or updated without a reference to the in-tree i18n README for that locale.
rationale: The in-tree README holds the authoritative rationale for locale-specific choices; omitting a cross-reference risks duplicating or contradicting that guidance.
